AMGN.letter_by: Robert A. Bradway, Chairman and CEO
AMGN.letter: Amgen says it now serves about 17 million patients and calls its strategy consistent: innovation plus disciplined execution. Profit rose sharply in 2025 from a weak 2024, and the company kept paying down the debt it took on to buy Horizon Therapeutics.
pipeline: MariTide (monthly-or-less obesity shot): six global Phase 3 studies underway; 2026 is a data-generation year
Repatha: Phase 3 VESALIUS-CV showed fewer heart attacks and strokes in high-risk patients without a prior event
IMDELLTRA: full FDA approval in Nov 2025 for small cell lung cancer after the DeLLphi-304 study
Setback: bemarituzumab will not be filed in first-line gastric cancer (Feb 2026)
AMGN.debt_reason: Debt fell about $5.5B as Amgen kept repaying the money it borrowed in 2023 to buy Horizon Therapeutics, a growth acquisition.

segment_moats.note: Denosumab patents expired in 2025 and biosimilars have launched, so this moat is eroding.
Patent-protected cholesterol drug; the VESALIUS-CV outcome data widen its use.
Patent-protected oral psoriasis drug.
Patents run to 2029, but Medicare price negotiation cut sales about 33% last year.
Patent-protected bone-building drug.
The only approved drug for thyroid eye disease.
Same molecule as Prolia, so it faces the same biosimilar erosion.

AMGN.segment_moats_basis: Claude's assessment of each business line against Morningstar's five moat sources (intangible assets, switching costs, network effect, cost advantage, efficient scale), from the company's 10-K and the research sources listed.

CAT.letter: Caterpillar's centennial year brought the highest sales and revenues in its history (about $67.6B, up 4%), but tariffs and costs squeezed margins, so profit per share fell to $18.81 from $22.05. The refreshed strategy has three pillars: Commercial Excellence, Advanced Technology Leader, and Transform How We Work.
pipeline: Autonomous mining machines and fleet-management technology (Resource Industries)
Power generation for data centers: engines and turbines riding AI demand
More capacity: capital spending rose about 33% in 2025
CAT.debt_reason: Most of the increase sits in Cat Financial (up $3.8B), which borrows to fund the loans and leases customers use to buy equipment. That is normal for its finance arm, not a sign of stress. Buybacks plus dividends (about $8B) also ran above free cash flow (about $7.5B).

segment_moats.note: Trusted brand, a large installed base of engines and turbines that needs Cat parts and service, and manufacturing scale.
Brand, the largest dealer network for parts and service, and scale.
Mining fleets and autonomy systems are hard to switch, and only a few companies build large mining trucks.
Cheap funding thanks to the parent's credit rating; mainly supports equipment sales.

GLW.letter_by: Wendell P. Weeks, Chairman and CEO
GLW.letter: Corning calls its Springboard plan a 'tremendous success' two years in. Core sales rose 13% to $16.4B, core EPS rose 29%, and adjusted free cash flow nearly doubled. The company raised its high-confidence target to $4B of added annual sales by end of 2026 and set goals of a $30B run rate by 2028 and $40B by 2030.
pipeline: Optical connectivity for AI data centers (Gen AI fiber and cable)
Hemlock solar: polysilicon and US-made solar modules ramping (Q4 sales up 62%)
Adding capacity and technology for Springboard, with customers sharing the cost and risk
GLW.debt_reason: Growth. The rise came mainly from finance leases for new capacity (up to $869M from $144M) and new Chinese yuan loans that Corning says fund capital investment, with spending up 33%.

segment_moats.note: Fiber process know-how and patents, scale, and qualified-supplier status with data-center customers.
Proprietary fusion glass process in a market with only a few suppliers.
Gorilla Glass brand and patents, designed into phones years ahead.
Emissions-control substrate technology.
Lab products in a competitive market; no clear moat.
Solar polysilicon is a commodity; trade protection, not a moat, supports it.

KLAC.letter: Revenue rose 12% to $13.58B (product +10%, services +16%). KLA says it sits on the 'critical path' of the AI build-out, with high-bandwidth memory and advanced packaging driving new demand. The board approved a higher dividend and $7B more for buybacks, and management expects momentum to speed up into 2027.
pipeline: Advanced-packaging process control, which KLA expects to top about $1.1B in calendar 2026 (up 70%+)
Inspection and metrology for leading-edge AI chips and HBM
KLAC.debt_reason: Debt was flat. Buybacks and dividends were paid from free cash flow (about $3.8B).

segment_moats.note: Leading share in process control; tools are built into fab process recipes, and few rivals compete.
Service on a large installed base of KLA tools, with high renewal rates.
Metrology for advanced lithography, qualified into customer processes.
Niche deposition and etch tools.
Former Orbotech line; more competitive than the core business.

RTX.letter_by: Christopher T. Calio, Chairman and CEO
RTX.letter: Sales rose 10% to $88.6B and free cash flow reached $7.9B. Over $138B of new orders lifted backlog 23% to a record $268B ($161B commercial, $107B defense). The 2026 focus is new capabilities, more production capacity and working down the backlog; guidance is $92-93B in sales.
pipeline: GTF Advantage engine certified by the FAA and EASA (4-8% more takeoff thrust, up to 1% less fuel)
GTF repair network expanded to 21 sites (shop visits up 26%)
Raytheon missile and air-defense capacity expansion
RTX.debt_reason: Debt fell about $3.4B as RTX repaid borrowings from operating cash.

segment_moats.note: Decades of aftermarket service on engines in use, certified designs, and only a few engine makers worldwide.
Certified components built into aircraft platforms for their whole life.
Few defense primes, classified technology, and multi-decade government programs.

UNH.letter: This is a turnaround year. Hemsley came back after Andrew Witty stepped down, promised to change leadership, culture, practices and board oversight, and asked shareholders for patience. Medical costs rose faster than expected, so profit fell again even as revenue grew 12%. He guided to 'solid but moderate' earnings growth for 2026 and stronger growth after that.
pipeline: Repricing Medicare Advantage and exiting unprofitable plans
Fixing Optum Health's performance, which management says has not met expectations
Technology- and data-driven care at Optum
UNH.debt_reason: Debt was roughly flat (up 2%). Acquisitions, buybacks and dividends were covered by about $16B of free cash flow.

segment_moats.note: Scale to negotiate provider prices, and the breadth of its provider network.
Purchasing scale with drug makers and pharmacies.
Software and data built into hospital and insurer workflows.
Under repair; management says it has not met expectations, and there is no clear moat yet.
